note:
THE CANONICAL BOX'S REPO CANNOT GARBAGE-COLLECT, AND HAS NOT FOR SOME TIME. Noticed as a warning git prints on ordinary fetches; recorded rather than fixed, because the fix must not run while the box is busy.

    $ cat .git/gc.log
    warning: There are too many unreachable loose objects; run 'git prune' to remove them.

    $ git count-objects -v
    count: 6727          <- loose objects
    size: 141507         <- 141 MB loose
    in-pack: 119645
    size-pack: 1729081

    $ du -sh .git
    1.8G

WHAT gc.log DOES: while that file exists, git REFUSES to run automatic gc — it
assumes the last attempt failed and declines to retry. So every fetch prints the
warning and nothing reclaims anything. The loose objects accumulate; 141 MB of
them so far.

WHY IT IS NOT SAFE TO FIX RIGHT NOW: `git prune` deletes unreachable objects,
and this repository is written continuously by chamber jobs, censuses and heavy
runs from the shared claim. Pruning concurrently with a process that is creating
objects is the documented race — an object written but not yet referenced looks
exactly like garbage. A job is holding the staff as I write this.

THE SAFE PROCEDURE, for whoever does it, on an IDLE box:

    bash scripts/census-run.sh status   # must report no holder
    git prune                           # default 2-week grace; do NOT pass --expire=now
    rm -f .git/gc.log                   # let automatic gc resume
    git count-objects -v                # confirm `count` fell

The default two-week grace is the safety: an object younger than that survives
even if unreachable, which covers anything a live session is mid-way through.
`--expire=now` removes that protection and should not be used here.

CONTRIBUTING CAUSE, PARTLY MINE: I removed nine orphaned worktrees earlier
today (35 GB reclaimed), which detached whatever those checkouts referenced. The
count was already high — gc has been blocked long enough to accumulate 6,727 —
but the removals will have added to it. Worth knowing that the cleanup has a
second-order cost that shows up here rather than in `df`.
